summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old female with a history of type I diabetes, end-stage renal disease with prior kidney and pancreas transplants, and severe mitral regurgitation was admitted for worsening heart failure symptoms, primarily fatigue and dyspnea. She underwent elective cardiac catheterization, which revealed two-vessel coronary artery disease with a 90% proximal LAD stenosis and 80% RCA lesions, confirming chronic inferior ischemia as the cause of her mitral regurgitation. Due to the extent of disease, she was scheduled for coronary artery bypass grafting and mitral valve replacement. Her renal function remained stable with protective hydration, and no dialysis was required. She was discharged home with medication adjustments, including increased aspirin and reduced ranitidine, and instructions to monitor weight and prepare for upcoming surgery.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
